About Menlo Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale.

We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place. The Role We are looking for a Robotics Technician to help bring Asimov to life in the flesh.

This role is for someone who likes getting their hands dirty: assembling electronics, welding brackets, crimping harnesses, and debugging CAN networks. You will work directly on cutting-edge robotic hardware, catching design flaws before they become field failures and turning drawings into a real, working humanoid. What You'll Do
Perform precise mechanical and electrical integration: harness routing, PCB soldering, cable crimping, and component installation
Identify mechanical and design flaws during assembly to improve reliability and scalability
Build and test custom mounts, fixtures, and test rigs under tight timelines
Support construction of the final robot platform as components arrive over the coming months
Troubleshoot systems using automotive-style diagnostic methods
Document every step clearly, including photo evidence tied to tickets or Linear workflows
Maintain workshop cleanliness, organize build zones, and keep operations safe and compliant
Work autonomously with minimal oversight, but hold a high bar for quality
What We Look For
Hands-on experience in mechanical fabrication and electronic circuitry
Confident reading wiring schematics and interpreting layout drawings
Proficient with hand tools, power tools, multimeters, and basic CAD views
Skilled in harness prep, termination, and routing (crimping, heat-shrink, connectors)
Comfortable with iterative rework and iteration-based problem solving
Passionate about clean documentation and reproducible processes
Prior experience in automotive, industrial equipment, or robotics fields

Familiarity with CAN bus communication and protocol analysis
Experience with chassis integration or vehicle-scale systems
Knowledge of torque specs, tolerance stacking, and structural integrity checks
Exposure to startup-paced product cycles
Why Join Menlo You will be part of a tight-knit team defining the next generation of humanoid robots. With genuine ownership of the build and the freedom to solve problems your own way, you will see the hardware you touch come to life in real-world deployments.

If you thrive in fast-paced, open, collaborative environments, let's build the future of robotics together. A Note on AI You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. Equal Opportunity and Accommodations We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds.

If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

[Space Research and Planetary Sciences](https://www.space.unibe.ch)

The Space Research and Planetology Division at the University of Bern researches the formation and evolution of our solar system. For this purpose, among other things, highly specialized instruments are developed and built for spacecraft, which subsequently carry out measurements in situ, e.g. in the vicinity of Jupiter.

Our team is internationally recognized for its achievements and cooperates in numerous space missions, with, for example, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the American space agency, NASA.

On top of space-related activities, our Division is also involved in flagship projects for ground-based astronomy, such as for the European 39-m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT).

In this context, we were recently awarded funding to develop an adaptive optics (AO) system for the 80-cm telescope of the Zimmerwald Observatory, in collaboration with the Astronomical Institute of the University of Bern (AIUB) and EPFL. To help meet these challenges, we are now seeking an experienced Automation Technician (Automatiker) HF/FH.
The position is available starting soon, or upon negotiation, for an initial period of one year with the option of extension. Our salary range is determined in accordance with the personnel regulations of the Canton of Bern.
**Tasks**
Your focus will be on the concept of hardware and software development of PLC Systems, in particular in the context of an adaptive optics real-time system for a ground-based telescope.

* Electrical concept and system definition, including the design of electrical schematics
* System and subsystem preparation, assembly, and cabling
* System and Sub-system programming on PLC System (Beckhoff)
* Interface programming for testing and script development (Python)
* System and Sub-system, hardware integration, testing, verification and validation
* Creating and maintaining the required documentation

* Automation Technician (Automatiker) HF/FH or equivalent engineering B.Sc.
* Experience in programming Beckhoff PLCs and developing test scripts using Python.
* Experience in C/C++ software development would be an advantage.
* Good spoken and written knowledge of English is required. German would be an advantage.

We are seeking a driven technician (m/f/d) with proven hands-on experience in mechanical assembly, soldering, desoldering, wire harnesses, and troubleshooting mechanical and electronic tasks. In this role, you will support and maintain existing products to ensure they remain fully operational and improve and develop new solutions for robust hardware.
Success in this role requires both technical excellence and the ability to adapt and make decisions under uncertainty.

Ensure that the robotics systems are ready to be used at all times
Create detailed documentation, technical drawings, and assembly instructions for testing rigs or needed components
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (mechanical, software, manufacturing) to ensure seamless system integration
Maintain Bill of Materials (BOM), assembly instructions, and quality control documentation, support and creation of SOPs
Troubleshoot and resolve mechanics and electronics issues during development and production phases
Stay updated with emerging technologies and best practices in robotics and mechanical/electronics design
Perform assembly and disassembly of robots components, cables, and PCBs and other devices
Carry out soldering, desoldering, wiring, and basic troubleshooting tasks (e.g. oscilloscope, signal analyzers)
Support procurement activities by identifying suitable products which meet requirements, sourcing suppliers, and obtaining quotations
Open to travel to China for business trips
The role involves significant travel (approximately 50%) to client sites
Work autonomously on open-ended, evolving tasks
Essential Skills
Hands-on experience with soldering SMD components
Proficiency in Altium / Solidworks is recommended
Proficiency in English, Spoken and written
Knowledge of electronics design principles
Knowledge of actuators and sensors using robotics, familiarity with sensor integration (force/torque sensors, encoders, IMUs) is recommended
Hands-on experience with rapid prototyping (3D printing, CNC machining, laser cutting) is recommended
Able to find fast solutions to common problems
Beneficial Skills
Minimum 3-5 years of proven work experience in related fields
Experience in robotics, mechatronics, or automation industries
Background in designing robust cabling solutions and cable harnesses
Familiarity with electronics design and PCB production stages

Agile Robots SE is an international high-tech company based in Munich, Germany with a production site in Kaufbeuren and more than 3500 employees worldwide.

Our mission is to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and robotics by developing systems that combine state-of-the-art force-moment-sensing and world-leading image-processing technology. This unique combination of technologies allows us to provide user-friendly and affordable robotic solutions that enable intelligent precision assembly.
This is made possible by our employees, who bring out the best in each and every day with creativity and enthusiasm. Become part of this team and shape the future of robotics with us!
We are proud of our diversity and welcome your application regardless of gender and sexual identity, nationality, ethnicity, religion, age, or disability.
